PRINCIPLE: Tests should focus on a single behavior. RATIONALE: Single Arrange-Act-Assert helps pinpoint failures. EVALUATION: The method performs exactly one operation (constructor call) and contains a single Act. DECISION: Only one Act operation present -> compliant. VERDICT: The test is atomic; it contains a single operation (new MaxMin3()) with one logical block.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should not share mutable state. RATIONALE: Independence enables reordering/parallel runs. EVALUATION: The method uses only a local variable and does not reference or modify static/instance fields or rely on other tests. DECISION: No shared mutable state seen in the method -> compliant. VERDICT: Based solely on the method body it is independent.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Both happy path and error scenarios should be tested. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness. EVALUATION: The class (and this method) only contains a single happy-path-like construct; there is no test covering an error/exception case. DECISION: No exception tests or multiple test methods covering error flows -> non-compliant. VERDICT: The test suite lacks an exceptional-flow test for the functionality under test.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should check min/max/edge inputs. RATIONALE: Boundaries reveal off-by-one errors. EVALUATION: The method only constructs an object (no input domain or numeric parameters). DECISION: The method under test (constructor with no args) does not present an obvious boundary domain -> not-applicable. VERDICT: Boundary analysis is not relevant to this specific test method.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained with helper methods for repeated logic. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication. EVALUATION: The single test is very short (<10 lines) and contains no duplicated blocks. DECISION: Short standalone test with no repetition -> compliant. VERDICT: For this method modularity is acceptable given its brevity.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and simple. RATIONALE: Easier to maintain and less error-prone. EVALUATION: The method is very short (few lines), contains no loops or conditionals. DECISION: Under complexity thresholds and linear flow -> compliant. VERDICT: The test meets the small/low-complexity requirement.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties. RATIONALE: Superficial assertions may miss faults. EVALUATION: There are no assertions at all in this method (no verification of properties). DECISION: Only construction is performed with zero assertions -> non-compliant. VERDICT: The test does not assert any properties to detect faults.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored/commented-out tests. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide problems. EVALUATION: No @Ignore or @Disabled annotations, no commented-out @Test methods in the provided method/class snippet. DECISION: No evidence of ignored or commented tests -> compliant. VERDICT: The test is active and runnable.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should reference requirements. RATIONALE: Enables traceability to requirements. EVALUATION: Class-level Javadoc contains 'Requirement traceability: REQ-MAXMIN3-001', providing traceability. DECISION: Presence of REQ- prefix in class comment -> compliant. VERDICT: Traceability information is present at the class level.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security tests are separate. RATIONALE: Usually not applicable for small unit tests. EVALUATION: No performance/security tests are expected for this simple constructor test and none are present. DECISION: For a basic unit test this practice is usually not-applicable -> not-applicable. VERDICT: No performance/security testing is expected here.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should be descriptive. RATIONALE: Improves self-documentation. EVALUATION: The method is named 'test6', which is generic and does not describe the scenario or expected outcome. DECISION: Generic naming detected -> non-compliant. VERDICT: Name should be improved to reflect behavior under test.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid verbose auto-generated tests. RATIONALE: Generated tests can be hard to maintain. EVALUATION: The test class uses EvoSuite runner and the test name 'test6' is typical of generated tests. DECISION: Evidence of automatic-generation patterns (EvoSuite runner and generic test name) -> non-compliant. VERDICT: The class shows signs of heavy generation and could be simplified.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Prioritization of Test Case Design
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should show thoughtful design (Given-When-Then or BDD naming). RATIONALE: TDD/BDD improves coverage. EVALUATION: The single minimal test lacks Given-When-Then structure or multiple scenario coverage; it appears written after-the-fact. DECISION: Minimal/basic test only -> non-compliant. VERDICT: Test design lacks evidence of prioritization or BDD-style structure.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests should use public APIs and avoid implementation details. RATIONALE: Behavior-based tests are maintainable. EVALUATION: The method simply calls a public constructor and does not access private fields or use reflection. DECISION: Only public API used -> compliant. VERDICT: The test interacts with public behavior rather than internals.

PRINCIPLE: Use specific assertions with messages. RATIONALE: Specific assertions aid diagnosis. EVALUATION: The test contains NO assertions at all; therefore assertions are not used adequately. DECISION: Zero assertions -> non-compliant. VERDICT: Add specific assertions (assertEquals/assertNotNull with messages) to improve fault detection.

PRINCIPLE: Comments should explain 'why' not 'what' and avoid commented-out code. RATIONALE: Excessive comments are harmful. EVALUATION: There is class-level Javadoc documenting purpose and requirement traceability; no commented-out code in the method. DECISION: Comments are appropriate and no commented-out code is present -> compliant. VERDICT: Documentation at class-level is useful; method is clean.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should avoid randomness/time/external dependencies. RATIONALE: Determinism prevents flaky tests. EVALUATION: The method uses no Random, time, Thread.sleep, or external resources; it only constructs an object. DECISION: No sources of non-determinism detected -> compliant. VERDICT: The test is deterministic based on its code.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Tests must not leave persistent side effects. RATIONALE: Side effects create inter-test dependencies. EVALUATION: The method does not create files, DB entries, or modify static state; only a local object is created. DECISION: No side effects present -> compliant. VERDICT: The test is side-effect free.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Suitable Utilization of Test Labels and Categories
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Use categories/tags to organize tests. RATIONALE: Enables selective execution. EVALUATION: The class is annotated with @Category(UnitTest.class). DECISION: Category annotation present at class level -> compliant. VERDICT: Tests are categorized appropriately.
